bk_22.subject: Tight head-and-shoulders close-up at eye level, the face large and filling the upper half of the picture, of a young man looking straight into the lens: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt, rolled-up red trousers, barefoot, a round bronze medallion on a cord around his neck, calm and searching, one hand holding a torn half of a small plain blank cream paper, nothing printed or written on it, up beside his cheek, a thumb and four fingers on that hand. One person in the picture. Only head, shoulders and chest in the picture, no legs. His face in the upper third of the picture.
bk_22.setting: a wide trampled dirt yard among nipa huts on stilts, a big old wooden barn and bamboo groves in the countryside north of Manila, on a night in August 1896, hundreds of flaming torches; no modern buildings, no electric wires, no guns
bk_22.light: soft warm torchlight, falling scraps of paper out of focus behind, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
